rationale: A wins because it finds the real tension and keeps the receipts nearby: "Oatly cuts the carbon footprint of its barista oat milk by 31% while closing a US plant" is an actual business story, not launch confetti. B has usable bones, but "Oatly wins its biggest pour-volume deal" invents "biggest" and turns a 1,400-location default into a swagger claim the update never supplied. A has one overextended pricing angle, but it mostly names the holes instead of wallpapering over them.
gaps_in_A: "A 1,400-store coffee chain makes oat milk the default, not the upcharge" implies an upcharge/no-upcharge story the facts do not provide; the update only says default non-dairy option and no retail price change.

"Oatly reformulated and held the price. Someone is absorbing the difference." assumes margin pressure or changed input cost. That may be the right question, but the update does not say the reformulation costs more or less.
"Reformulations usually travel with a price move in one direction or the other" is a broad industry claim dropped in without evidence. It needs proof or it reads like convenient setup.

The next step says, "If the LCA report and a named chain contact are not obtainable this week...pitch only the foodservice angle," but the foodservice angle collapses without a named chain contact. That sentence trips over its own logic.
gaps_in_B: "Oatly wins its biggest pour-volume deal" is invented. The update gives 1,400 locations, not biggest, not volume, and not a ranking against prior Oatly deals.
"shifts pour volume" is a plausible consequence, not a supplied fact. Without volume, mix, or ordering data, this is the sort of little embellishment that gets a pitch killed on reply two.
The customer-story angle lists "no price change at retail" under facts it rests on, but retail pricing does not prove anything about a coffee-chain foodservice rollout.

"The retail angle...is a non-event" throws away a possible business-margin question too fast. Shopper impact is weak, yes; retail buyer/category economics alongside losses and plant closure is not automatically dead.
